name: crypto-ecb-mode-block-cipher
attack_scenario: Attacker observing ECB ciphertext of a structured record (e.g. an auth cookie or ECB-encrypted image) recovers repeated blocks and can cut-and-paste ciphertext blocks to forge a valid message without the key.
negative_test_hint: encrypt the repeated-block plaintext "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA" and assert the ciphertext has no repeated 16-byte blocks, which ECB would echo

exemplar.explanation: ECB encrypts identical plaintext blocks to identical ciphertext blocks, leaking the structure of the data and letting an attacker cut and paste ciphertext blocks to forge a valid message without the key. GCM (or any mode with a random IV and authentication) provides semantic security and integrity, so repeated plaintext blocks never repeat in ciphertext.
